title: regression-risk-budgeting-scenarios
content:
Purpose:
Short working doc to define how we budget eval spend for cheaper-config rollouts and attach concrete gating rules for automatic/semiautomatic blocking. Goal is to produce a spreadsheet template + a small decision matrix we can operationalize in Optimize.

High-level constraints / assumptions (working):
- We want to allow ~20–40% unit-cost reduction moves (quantization + smaller base model variants) without manual full-eval for every change.
- Tolerable quality regressions must be bounded; some narrow regressions acceptable if user-impact low.
- Eval compute budget is finite: target monthly eval budget per team = $X (placeholder in sheet).
- Real user impact = function(traffic_share, regression_severity, time-to-detect) — we approximate via surrogate eval metrics.

Definitions and signals we will use (spreadsheet columns):
- config_id: internal short id for a candidate config
- model_variant: name (e.g., redwood-7b-q4_0)
- quant_profile: descriptive (q4_0, q8_1, int8-fp16-mix)
- expected_token_cost_per_req: derived from perf traces (tokens * $/token variant)
- baseline_quality_score: reference metric (composite, see below)
- candidate_quality_score: same metric run on our eval sets
- delta_quality_abs: baseline - candidate (positive = candidate worse)
- delta_quality_pct: percent drop relative to baseline
- high_risk_fail_rate: fraction of critical prompts below pass threshold
- eval_sample_cost: cost to run the candidate over our standardized eval set
- projected_monthly_savings: (baseline_cost - candidate_cost) * projected_volume
- expected_user_impact_cost: proxy cost = delta_quality_pct * impact_weight * projected_volume * value_per_request
- net_expected_savings = projected_monthly_savings - expected_user_impact_cost - eval_sample_cost
- rollout_category: auto-allow / soft-gate / hard-block

Composite quality score (proposal):
- Weighted average of: pass_rate_on_critical_prompts (50%), mean_nll_on_holdout (20%), rerank_precision@5 (15%), hallucination_indicator (15%).
- The weights are provisional — sheet has a quick sensitivity tab.

Gating rules (first-pass thresholds):
- Auto-allow: delta_quality_pct <= 0.5% AND high_risk_fail_rate delta <= 0.1% AND eval_sample_cost < 1% of monthly eval budget.
- Soft-gate (canary + human review): 0.5% < delta_quality_pct <= 1.5% OR high_risk_fail_rate delta <= 0.5%. Requires 7-day canary at 0.5% traffic, automated daily checks; if metrics worsen by > 2x from canary baseline, auto-rollback.
- Hard-block: delta_quality_pct > 1.5% OR high_risk_fail_rate delta > 0.5% OR any hallucination_indicator jump > 20%. Hard-block prevents rollout beyond internal test traffic.
- Emergency override: product/security can temporarily block or permit; override must be logged and include rollback plan.

Spreadsheet strategy and tabs (how to use):
- Tab A: master config registry (all candidate rows, serveable flags)
- Tab B: eval-run scheduler (links to jobs, cost estimate formulas)
- Tab C: sensitivity matrix (vary composite weights and show gate flips)
- Tab D: canary simulation (sample size calc, expected time-to-detect given effect size)
- Tab E: past incidents and lessons (linked PRs/tickets)

Example scenario (numbers illustrative):
- baseline: model cost per request = $0.012, candidate cost = $0.007 -> savings = $0.005 (~41%)
- monthly projected volume = 30M requests -> projected_monthly_savings = $150k
- eval_sample_cost: running standardized 10k prompt set = $140 (GPU + infra estimate)
- baseline_quality_score = 87.6, candidate_quality_score = 86.9 -> delta_quality_pct = 0.8%
- expected_user_impact_cost: assume value_per_request $0.0004 and impact_weight 0.8 -> ~ 0.8% * 0.8 * 30M * 0.0004 = $76.8k
- net_expected_savings = 150k - 76.8k - 0.14k = ~73.1k -> candidate looks attractive but falls into soft-gate (0.8%>0.5%), so require canary + 7-day monitoring.

Sampling & eval-cost controls (practical):
- Stratified sampling: ensure critical segments (billing, legal language, long-context threads) represented at >30% of eval weight even if rare in traffic.
- Progressive sampling: run a small quick-check (1k prompts) to filter obvious fails before full 10k run. Save that cost if rejected early.
- Reuse cached runs: if model_variant shares prefix cache or same quantization family, reuse partial eval artifacts (e.g., token-level alignments) to reduce compute.

Automation hooks we want in Optimize (asks for infra/engineering):
- Page that marks rollout_category based on a computed row formula; flag changes in Slack + console.
- Auto-scheduler that runs the prescribed eval sample and posts results.
- Canary guardrail: automatic daily re-eval and if delta_quality_pct growth rate > threshold -> trigger rollback.
- Cost delta simulator: quick UI to adjust projected_volume and value_per_request and see net_expected_savings.

Open questions / unknowns (needs follow-up):
- How do we pick value_per_request consistently across products? Suggested: partner with finance/product to assign ranges per product area (GTM teams already have LTV/ARPU proxies).
- How sensitive is the composite metric to outlier prompts? Do we need robust trimming?
- Are there regulatory/legal buckets where ANY regression >0 is unacceptable? (legal docs, financial disclosures) -> escalate to compliance for per-customer gating.
- Guardrails for long-tail emergent failures post-rollout (rare prompts not in eval set) — what's acceptable MTTD and MTTR?

Next steps (short):
- Jonah: build the spreadsheet template (Tab layout above) and populate with two historical candidates for backtest (due 2025-12-05).
- Priya: run sensitivity analysis on composite weights and return a one-page summary of flips (due 2025-12-08).
- AVA: draft a short PRD for the auto gating logic to hand to infra (initial draft 2025-12-10).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative on thresholds to start; we can loosen gates after 2–3 successful rollouts.
- Keep an eye on hallucination_indicator — it's noisy and benefits from ensemble signals (human labeling samples).
- If you add new columns to the sheet, note the formula in the header row.

Appendix: quick formulas (for copy into sheet):
- delta_quality_pct = (baseline_quality_score - candidate_quality_score) / baseline_quality_score * 100
- projected_monthly_savings = (baseline_cost_per_req - candidate_cost_per_req) * projected_volume
- expected_user_impact_cost = delta_quality_pct/100 * impact_weight * projected_volume * value_per_request
- net_expected_savings = projected_monthly_savings - expected_user_impact_cost - eval_sample_cost

-- end of draft --
